notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup (trial credits). Small CSaaS focused on SMB ecommerce merchants. Came in via blog post about cheap embeddings but pivoted to chat for triage bot.

Initial call (03/02) — tone: pragmatic, cost-sensitive. Reported user complaints about sluggish responses on live chat (users see long spinner). Key quote: "Feels like waiting for human on hold."

Observed behavior: p50 ~220ms, p95 ~820ms for text-generation calls to us-east1 default; jitter spikes during peak (11:30-13:30 PST). Mostly single-turn chat but includes 1–3 contextual system messages + 2–3 user messages (avg prompt length 600–1200 tokens including history).

Customer constraints/asks: keep data in public cloud, SOC2 compliance, cannot provision dedicated infra (budget). Wants <300ms median and <500ms p95 for short assistant replies. Very cost-sensitive — wants low token usage and fewer retries.

Perf troubleshooting notes from call:
- AE/SE suggested region switch (us-west1) and enabling streaming — customer worried about client changes.
- Tried lowering max_tokens and truncating history: reduced token usage by ~30% on sample, p95 improved to ~600ms but still above target.
- Timeout behavior: frontend sets HTTP timeout 10s and then reconnects; causes bad UX on long tails. Recommend bumping client timeout for streaming/keepalive and adding progressive UI.
- Prompt guidance: recommend tighter system prompts, compress context (summarize history every N turns), strip verbose templates. Provide 3 short templates (support-single-turn, quick-summary, escalation-handoff).
- Suggested model routing: use smaller faster model variant for short responses and fallback to larger for long/higher-quality answers. Customer wants help mapping which model to pick from Redwood catalog.

Sales notes / tone: early discovery — strong intent to continue evaluating but needs quick wins on latency. Likely to convert if p95 under 500ms and cost delta small.
